title: Characterizing Multi-Domain Representations for Gastric Histopathological Image Classification
abstract: This study presents FLIGENT-Net, a multi-domain signal representation framework for gastric histopathological image classification that treats tissue images as complex two-dimensional signals whose diagnostic content is distributed across spatial, spectral, relational, and contextual domains. Using the GasHisSDB dataset, FLIGENT-Net investigates spatial representations extracted through a convolutional neural network (CNN), frequency-domain information obtained using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), graph-based relational modeling through a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) acting as a graph-signal-processing operator, and global contextual modeling through a Vision Transformer (ViT). Rather than evaluating the framework solely according to classification accuracy, a systematic characterization was performed using individual and combined configurations, computational cost, training dynamics, interpretability, Pearson and Spearman correlation of importance maps, and Pixel Deletion analysis. FLIGENT-Net achieved 96.98% Accuracy, 95.45% Precision, 96.95% Recall, 96.20% F1-Score, and 0.9959 AUC-ROC. Notably, the simpler CNN+GCN configuration achieved a higher Accuracy of 97.76%, while CNN+GCN+FFT achieved 97.75%; this outcome shows that combining all four representation domains does not monotonically improve classification accuracy, reinforcing the characterization-oriented contribution of this study over a purely performance-driven one. The importance-map analysis revealed distinct patterns across representations, with low global Pearson and Spearman correlations. Pixel Deletion yielded a positive ∆AUC of 0.1450 for FLIGENT-Net. Overall, the results characterize distinct classification, computational, interpretability, and faithfulness profiles across multi-domain signal representations, offering a computational methods case study in spectral and graph-based image-signal analysis for biomedical applications.

title: Transfer Learning for Low-Shot Object Recognition in Remote Sensing
abstract: Low-shot object recognition with remote sensing has limitations such as insufficient labeled samples, large within-class differences, and complicated scenes structures. To this end, in this paper, we propose a transfer learning-based approach for recognition in few-shot settings with the use of pre-trained deep models. With the introduction of domain-adaptive feature extraction, attention-guided learning and geometric-aware encoding, the proposed method overcomes the deficiencies of previous methods, such as overfitting, computational complexity and lack of generalization. It shows that our model is very robust over various datasets and heavily reduces the training overhead in comparison with previous ones. This work opens up possibilities for deployable, reliable and efficient remote sensing in resource limited environment.

title: Integrating Q1RAM into Quantum Teleportation and Superdense Protocols: A Framework for Large-Scale Quantum Communications
abstract: Quantum teleportation and superdense coding are two different protocols that were developed to transmit a limited number of qubits and two classical bits, respectively. Therefore, they are inefficient for transmitting messages containing a massive number of individual qubits or classical bits. Thus, it is necessary to scale up these two protocols in larger systems to enable them to transmit massive messages. To achieve this goal, it is essential to integrate each of these two protocols within architectures that contain a quantum main memory that functions as a buffer capable of storing both quantum and classical data and managing a massive amount of data efficiently during transmission operations. Q1RAM is a cutting-edge quantum main memory and the fastest quantum main memory available, as it has a time complexity of $$O(1)$$ for accessing memory locations. In this paper, two architectural schematics are proposed based on integrating Q1RAM as a core component with the quantum teleportation and superdense coding protocols. The first architectural scheme is developed to scale up the quantum teleportation protocol, making it efficient for transmitting massive messages of separable individual qubits. The second architectural schema is proposed, consisting of two Q1RAM chips, two quantum processing units, two of the classical RAMs, and a quantum gateway. This proposed schema is developed to scale up the superdense coding protocol so that it can transmit massive classical messages containing large amounts of data. The experimental simulation results validate the architectural schematics for scaling up the quantum teleportation and the superdense coding protocols for large-scale quantum communications.

title: TaskGuard: Task-Conditioned Restoration Utility for Risk-Aware Object Detection
abstract: Image restoration is commonly applied before object detection under adverse conditions, yet a visually improved image need not improve the downstream task. We study this mismatch as restoration utility prediction: given a degraded image and its candidate restoration, should the restoration be used or should the original observation be preserved? We introduce TaskGuard, a post-hoc controller for frozen restoration and detection pipelines. TaskGuard characterizes the realized restoration residual through its interaction with detector sensitivity and predicts whether the intervention is task-beneficial. Exact regional counterfactuals reveal substantial within-image utility heterogeneity, while a deployable pseudo-gradient preserves statistically reliable directional information. Feature-group ablation further shows that task-conditioned evidence contributes information beyond detector-response and residual statistics. The TaskGuard utility predictor is trained only on Gaussian degradation and frozen before final evaluation, then transferred to unseen motion blur, rain, and defocus. Across these unseen families, TaskGuard reduces lossnegative interventions by 54.2% (family macro) and practical per-image detection deteriorations by 37.0% (pooled), while preserving 98.8% of the Always-Restore COCO AP. On natural-rain DAWN, it reduces loss-negative interventions by 97.9% while retaining 77.8% of the AP improvement obtained by deraining. These results support restoration utility as a task-conditioned property of the specific intervention rather than image appearance alone.

title: TRAIL: Trajectory-Aware Visual Place Recognition against Unordered Databases
abstract: Modern Visual Place Recognition (VPR) methods excel on standard benchmarks yet remain brittle in feature-poor environments. By treating each query image in isolation, they discard the sequential context in any real trajectory. We formalize a task that exploits this context: given a query sequence, localize the final image against an unordered reference database -- which, unlike sequence-to-sequence methods, requires no sequential structure in the database. We propose TRAIL (TRajectory-Aware Image Localization), a principled framework based on Conditional Random Fields (CRF) that combines learned functions for visual similarity and for camera-motion consistency, refining a distribution over candidate references as each query arrives. A lightweight post-processing layer atop any pre-trained VPR backbone, TRAIL improves a state-of-the-art baseline by up to 8.3 percentage points on our primary benchmark, transfers to unseen datasets without retraining, and delivers its largest gains where visual cues are scarce.

title: Single Image to Textured 3D Object Generation in Frequency Domain: From Theory to Pipeline
abstract: Single-view 3D reconstruction, also known as image-to-3D, is a persistently challenging task due to the extreme lack of information. Recently, diffusion models pre-trained on large-scale datasets served as 2D priors are used to solve the ill-posed task but suffer from color deviation and view inconsistency, which can be curbed by using diffusion models fine-tuned with 3D annotated data served as 3D priors. However, 3D priors lack high-frequency details, which cannot be solved by direct complementation with 2D priors in spatial domain for introducing erroneous low-frequency 2D prior guidance. In this paper, we revisit the characteristics of different diffusion priors from the frequency perspective. Based on our observations, we theoretically present a unified framework of hybrid optimization using multiple diffusion priors in frequency domain. Under this framework, we further propose Morpheus3D, a pipeline of 3D object generation from any single unposed image in the wild. Morpheus3D enhances 3D prior with high-pass image-prompt 2D prior guidance to reconstruct high-quality 3D objects while effectively suppressing view inconsistency, low-frequency color deviation, and high-frequency lacking problems. Both quantitative and qualitative experiments on the public and our collected datasets with complex textures show that our method exhibits significant improvements in generation quality.

title: From Clinical Free Text to Auditable Concepts: An Agentic Framework for Interpretable Prediction
abstract: Abstract Across application domains, predictive signals often sit in unstructured free text rather than structured fields, yet turning that text into useful and interpretable features is difficult. Running large language models (LLMs) over an entire corpus is costly and hard to reproduce, while end-to-end text representations can rely on surface cues that are difficult to inspect. We present an agentic workflow that takes a prediction task and a raw text corpus as input and produces an auditable feature layer. The first two agents use an LLM to derive a task-specific predictor taxonomy and weakly label a bounded text sample; routed local extractors then process the corpus, and a deterministic builder aggregates the evidence into a dynamic, longitudinal concept bottleneck. We evaluate the framework on medication discontinuation in a longitudinal oncology cohort and 30-day readmission in MIMIC-IV. With gradient boosting, the longitudinal bottleneck increases area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) over coarse concept buckets from 0.700 to 0.761 for medication discontinuation and from 0.576 to 0.609 for readmission. The proposed framework achieves predictive performance comparable to direct BioClinicalBERT prediction on both tasks while additionally providing explicit, interpretable, and traceable task-specific concepts. LLM use is confined to a bounded weak-labeling stage costing $24.00 and $23.39, respectively, compared with projected costs of $10,648 and $11,519 for exhaustive sentence-level LLM processing of the full corpora, demonstrating the substantial cost efficiency of the proposed agentic system.

title: Voice Recorder vs Dictaphone for Modern Productivity
authors: LTD Zhejiang Jinxun Digital Technology Co.
abstract: Many people still use the terms “voice recorder” and “dictaphone” interchangeably. However, modern recording technology has changed dramatically over the past few years, especially with the rise of AI note takers, AI voice recorders, and wearable AI recorders. Today’s users no longer want devices that simply store audio files. They want tools that can: transcribe conversations generate AI summaries organize meeting notes improve productivity workflows securely manage sensitive information As searches for ai recorder, ai voice recorder for meetings, and ai recorder note taker for lectures continue growing, understanding the difference between traditional dictation devices and modern AI-powered recorders becomes increasingly important.The Anypin Note Pod P1 represents this new generation of AI productivity tools designed for meetings, lectures, interviews, and everyday workflow management. What Is a Dictaphone? Originally, “Dictaphone” referred to a brand of dictation machines commonly used in offices, journalism, and legal environments. What Is a Dictaphone? AI Voice Recorder for Meetings Over time, the word became widely associated with traditional voice dictation devices designed mainly for: recording spoken notes office transcription workflows verbal memos administrative dictation Traditional dictaphones focused primarily on audio capture rather than intelligent organization. Most older dictation devices: stored recordings locally required manual playback depended on human transcription offered limited search functionality While useful at the time, these systems were built for a very different productivity era. What Is a Modern AI Voice Recorder? Modern ai note takers go far beyond basic audio recording. Instead of simply storing sound files, today’s AI note takers can: generate real-time transcripts summarize conversations automatically identify speakers create searchable notes organize meeting content support cloud synchronization This shift transforms recordings into usable knowledge rather than passive audio archives. Modern wearable AI recorders are especially popular among: professionals students consultants journalists researchers remote workers because they help reduce manual note-taking and improve productivity.. Voice Recorder vs Dictaphone: Key Differences Although both devices capture audio, their workflows and capabilities are very different. Feature Traditional Dictaphone Modern AI Voice Recorder Audio recording Yes Cell text AI transcription No Cell text AI summaries No Cell text Searchable transcripts No Yes Speaker recognition No Yes Cloud synchronization Limited Yes Workflow automation. Minimal Advanced Wearable portability Limited Common Data security features Basic Advanced Why AI Voice Recorders Are Replacing Traditional Dictation Devices The way people work has changed significantly. Today’s workflows involve: remote meetings hybrid collaboration online lectures fast-moving discussions mobile productivity multitasking environments Traditional dictation devices were not designed for these modern workflows. AI-powered recording systems are becoming more popular because they help users: capture conversations faster organize information automatically review notes more efficiently reduce manual documentation improve collaboration For many users, AI note-taking tools are now productivity systems rather than simple recording devices. Why Wearable AI Recorders Are Becoming More Popular One of the biggest trends in the recording industry is the rise of the wearable AI recorder category. Users increasingly want: lightweight devices hands-free recording discreet workflows mobile productivity quick recording access Compared to traditional dictaphones, wearable AI devices fit more naturally into: meetings classrooms interviews coworking spaces travel environments The wearable design of the Anypin Note Pod P1 helps support modern productivity workflows without interrupting conversations. Best Use Cases for Modern AI Note Takers Modern ai notetakers are now used across many industries and workflows. Meetings Professionals use AI voice recorders for meetings to: capture discussions organize action items summarize conversation improve follow-up workflows Lectures Professionals use AI voice recorders for meetings to: reduce note-taking pressure create searchable study materials review lessons faster Remote Work Remote teams use AI note-taking tools to: summarize virtual meetings improve asynchronous collaboration organize project discussions Data Security: Why Modern AI Recorders Need Strong Privacy Protection As AI recording tools become more powerful, privacy and security are becoming increasingly important. Traditional dictaphones were usually standalone offline devices. Modern AI note takers often involve: cloud synchronization AI processing discreet workflows searchable transcript management multi-device workflows This creates additional security considerations. Users increasingly search for: secure ai note taker encrypted ai recorder private AI meeting recorder secure AI transcription tools because recordings often contain: confidential meetings client discussions research interviews sensitive business information Why Data Full Protection Matters Modern AI productivity tools need stronger security frameworks to protect user information throughout the recording workflow. The Anypin Note Pod P1 emphasizes Data Full Protection with compliance support for: ISO/IEC 27001 ISO/IEC 27701 ISO/IEC 20000 ISO 56001 SOC 2 These standards help support: secure data management privacy-focused workflows encrypted information handling reliable system operations As AI productivity tools become more integrated into work and education, security is becoming one of the most important buying factors. Modern productivity workflows increasingly follow a simple AI-powered process: Record Capture conversations instantly during meetings, lectures, or interviews. Transcribe Convert audio into searchable text automatically. Summarize Generate AI-powered key points and action items. Organize Access and manage notes more efficiently across devices.This workflow is one reason modern AI recorders are replacing traditional dictation systems across many industries. Which Is Better: Dictaphone or AI Voice Recorder? For users who only need simple offline audio recording, traditional dictation devices may still work. However, for users who need: ISO/IEC 27001 ISO/IEC 27701 ISO/IEC 20000 ISO 56001 SOC 2 These standards help support: secure data management privacy-focused workflows encrypted information handling reliable system operations As AI productivity tools become more integrated into work and education, security is becoming one of the most important buying factors. Modern productivity workflows increasingly follow a simple AI-powered process: Record Capture conversations instantly during meetings, lectures, or interviews. Transcribe Convert audio into searchable text automatically. Summarize Generate AI-powered key points and action items. Organize Access and manage notes more efficiently across devices.This workflow is one reason modern AI recorders are replacing traditional dictation systems across many industries. Why Data Full Protection Matters Modern AI productivity tools need stronger security frameworks to protect user information throughout the recording workflow. The Anypin Note Pod P1 emphasizes Data Full Protection with compliance support for: searchable notes AI transcription workflow automation meeting summaries lecture organization productivity optimization secure cloud workflows modern AI voice recorders provide significantly more functionality.As work and education continue becoming more information-heavy, AI-powered note-taking systems are increasingly becoming essential productivity tools rather than optional accessories.For users looking for wearable portability, intelligent transcription, and strong Data Full Protection, the Anypin Note Pod P1 represents the next generation of AI-powered recording technology. FAQ What is the difference between a dictaphone and a voice recorder? A traditional dictaphone mainly records audio for manual playback and transcription, while modern AI voice recorders can also generate transcripts, summaries, searchable notes, and workflow automation. Are AI voice recorders better than traditional dictaphones? For productivity-focused workflows such as meetings, lectures, and interviews, AI voice recorders usually provide more advanced functionality and organization features. What is a wearable AI recorder? A wearable AI recorder is a compact device designed for hands-free audio recording and AI-powered transcription, often used for meetings, lectures, and mobile productivity. Why are AI note takers becoming popular? AI note takers help users reduce manual note-taking, organize information more efficiently, and improve productivity across meetings, lectures, and remote work. Is data security important for AI note takers? Yes. AI note takers often handle sensitive conversations, making secure storage, encrypted workflows, and privacy protection increasingly important. What security standards does the Anypin Note Pod P1 support? The Anypin Note Pod P1 supports compliance with ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, ISO/IEC 20000, ISO 56001, and SOC 2. Can AI note takers generate meeting summaries automatically? Yes. Many modern AI note takers can automatically generate summaries, transcripts, and action items from recorded conversations.

title: 基于自适应的领域自动微分算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to domain automatic differentiation (DAD) that leverages adaptive parameter adjustment to enhance computational efficiency, particularly within high-dimensional and non-linear domains. Traditional DAD methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness in complex data scenarios. We propose a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism inspired by the simulation of the differentiation process itself. This mechanism dynamically adjusts the parameters of the differential operators based on the input data characteristics and the resulting output, resulting in significantly improved performance in these challenging domains. The algorithm's core mechanism involves simulating the differentiation process and iteratively refining the parameter values to achieve optimal results. This work addresses limitations of existing DAD techniques by offering a more robust and adaptable approach capable of handling intricate data patterns.

title: Dynamic Programming for Online Learning with Delayed Feedback
abstract: Online learning aims to learn optimal policies from sequential feedback signals. Traditional online learning algorithms often falter when feedback is delayed or sparse, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper presents a novel approach to online learning that leverages dynamic programming (DP) to effectively handle delayed feedback. We adapt DP algorithms by incorporating a memory mechanism, enabling the system to store past states and rewards. This allows the algorithm to make decisions based on a broader historical context, significantly improving performance in scenarios with delayed or sparse feedback. The core claim is that DP's ability to consider future rewards, combined with a memory component, offers a robust and efficient solution compared to standard online learning methods. We provide a theoretical framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach and highlight its potential for applications where delayed feedback is prevalent. The key contribution is a more reliable and scalable method for learning in dynamic environments with imperfect information.

title: Biological Neural Networks: A Computational Complexity Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the computational complexity of biological neural networks, aiming to understand their inherent computational capabilities and efficiency. We translate the structural and functional characteristics of biological neural networks into formal computational models, then apply the tools of computational complexity theory to analyze these models. Specifically, we explore the relationship between network architecture (number of neurons, connectivity patterns, activation functions) and the computational complexity of tasks performed by the network. Our analysis focuses on classifying tasks based on their computational difficulty and identifying potential bottlenecks within the network's architecture that contribute to computational limitations. The results provide a theoretical framework for evaluating and potentially designing more efficient neural networks, bridging the gap between biological plausibility and computational performance. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of how biological systems achieve complex computations.

title: Title: Emergent Information Theory for Cryptography
abstract: This paper explores the application of emergent information theory to cryptography, proposing a novel theoretical framework centered on the observation and quantification of complex, dynamic system behavior as the source of information. Traditional cryptographic methods rely on the discrete and predictable nature of bits, but this research posits that information itself possesses a capacity for self-organization and patterns, leading to a security model based on these emergent properties. We outline a system for analyzing system data using statistical methods to identify and quantify these patterns, aiming to develop a cryptographic system that is resilient to reverse engineering through brute force and adversarial attacks. The core mechanism involves a dynamic analysis of system behavior, utilizing statistical measures to detect and characterize patterns that deviate significantly from expected behavior, thereby creating an inherently difficult-to-reverse-engineer encryption key. This approach moves beyond the limitations of traditional cryptographic algorithms by focusing on the underlying system rather than relying on the inherent properties of discrete symbols.

title: Neural Structured Memory Coding (NSMC)
abstract: This paper introduces Neural Structured Memory Coding (NSMC), a novel approach to neural network training and inference that addresses the limitations of traditional, often unstructured, representations of neural memory. The core claim of NSMC is that by transforming neural memory encoding into a structure amenable to parallel computation, significantly improved training efficiency and inference performance can be achieved. The central mechanism involves leveraging information theory and graph theory to represent connections and activation patterns between neurons as a graph structure. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are then employed for node embedding and relational reasoning within this graph. This structured approach offers the potential for enhanced interpretability, controllability, and optimization of neural networks, representing a shift from the inherent opacity of conventional neural memory representations. The key innovations lie in the formalization of this structured encoding and the integration of GNNs for effective processing. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual frameworks, the potential benefits of NSMC, paving the way for future research and development in this area.

title: Title: Contextualized Quantum Simulation with Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum simulation is a crucial tool for understanding complex quantum systems, but its implementation often faces challenges related to computational cost and accuracy. Static simulation methods struggle to adapt to the intricacies of the simulation, limiting fidelity and efficiency. This paper introduces a novel contextualized quantum simulation framework that dynamically adjusts the simulation parameters based on observed data. We propose an adaptive parameter tuning scheme leveraging statistical properties of the simulation's trajectory and progress. This approach significantly enhances the fidelity and efficiency of quantum simulations compared to traditional static methods, offering a pathway towards more powerful and practical quantum computations.

title: Formalization of Intuition as a Computational Process
abstract: Intuition, often described as a gut feeling or immediate understanding without conscious reasoning, remains a significant challenge for computational modeling. This paper proposes a formalization of intuition as a computational process, leveraging probabilistic inference and pattern recognition techniques. The core idea is to construct a system that simulates the human cognitive process of intuition, using Bayesian networks and related probabilistic models to represent beliefs and guide decision-making in situations characterized by incomplete information. The model aims to capture the underlying mechanisms of intuition by translating subjective experiences into quantifiable probabilistic relationships. This work outlines a framework for building such a system, emphasizing the role of Bayesian networks in representing uncertainty and facilitating intuitive judgments. The developed model offers a novel approach to understanding and potentially replicating human intuition within a computational context.

We propose a dynamically adjusting ANN architecture that automatically refines the graph's topology based on real-time data, thereby enhancing graph performance. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive learning process, enabling the network to continuously adjust the graph's connectivity and node representations. We demonstrate the efficacy of this algorithm through a series of benchmark graph tasks, showcasing its ability to maintain high accuracy and efficiency even with dynamically changing graph characteristics.

title: Topological Optimization of Quantum Algorithm Compilation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm compilation focused on topological optimization. Traditional quantum algorithm compilation methods primarily operate at the circuit level, neglecting the underlying topological constraints of quantum hardware. This limitation often leads to suboptimal circuit layouts and reduced execution efficiency. Our proposed methodology addresses this issue by translating quantum algorithms into topological graphs and subsequently utilizing topological optimization algorithms – such as shortest path algorithms and minimum cut algorithms – to intelligently refine the circuit layout. The core claim is to design an algorithm that automatically adapts to the specific topology of the quantum hardware, thereby maximizing the performance of the quantum algorithm. We explore the theoretical foundations and present a framework for this process, emphasizing the potential to significantly improve quantum algorithm execution speed and fidelity. The work represents a fundamental shift in quantum compilation, moving beyond circuit-centric approaches to a topology-aware paradigm.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Logic Programming with Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic logic programming that leverages Bayesian networks to bridge the gap between symbolic reasoning and neural network learning. Existing neuro-symbolic systems often face challenges in effectively integrating these two paradigms, leading to suboptimal performance. Our proposed system represents symbolic rules as Bayesian networks, allowing a neural network to learn the associated probabilities. This enables both deductive reasoning through Bayesian inference and probabilistic learning via the neural network. We demonstrate the core claim that this integration significantly improves the system's ability to handle complex logical problems. The system's architecture and methodology are described in detail, outlining the key components and their interactions. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of the approach, emphasizing the advantages of using Bayesian networks for representing and reasoning with symbolic knowledge. The approach offers a pathway towards more robust and interpretable AI systems capable of combining the strengths of both symbolic and connectionist paradigms. The core mechanism focuses on allowing the neural network to learn the conditional probability distributions within the Bayesian network, enabling a more flexible and adaptive reasoning process. This work provides a foundational framework for future research in neuro-symbolic AI.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance and Differential Privacy via Blockchain
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, existing FL systems are vulnerable to various attacks, including model poisoning and Byzantine attacks, which can compromise model integrity and user privacy. This paper proposes a novel decentralized federated learning framework that leverages blockchain technology to address these vulnerabilities. The framework incorporates Byzantine fault tolerance mechanisms to detect and mitigate malicious participants, and differential privacy techniques to protect user data. By utilizing a blockchain-based architecture, the system achieves secure and reliable learning while maintaining data privacy. The core claim is that current federated learning systems are vulnerable to attacks. The proposed mechanism utilizes a blockchain-based architecture for decentralized federated learning, incorporating Byzantine fault tolerance – detecting and mitigating malicious participants – and differential privacy – protecting user data – ensuring secure and reliable learning. The system's architecture is designed to provide transparency, auditability, and resilience against attacks, leading to a more trustworthy and secure FL environment.

title: Smart Technologies for a Changing World: A Multidomain Study of AI Driven Transformation
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as a defining technological force reshaping industries, governance, and society at an unprecedented pace. While domain-specific AI applications have demonstrated remarkable success, a holistic understanding of AI's cross-domain transformation patterns, shared challenges, and transferable solutions remains fragmented across disciplinary silos. This paper presents a comprehensive multidomain study examining AI-driven transformation across six critical sectors: healthcare, manufacturing, finance, agriculture, education, and transportation. Through a mixed-methods approach combining systematic literature analysis of 850 publications (2020–2025), quantitative performance benchmarking across 42 AI deployment case studies, and a survey of 1,680 industry practitioners and policymakers across 28 countries, we develop the SMART-AI (Systematic Multidomain Assessment of Responsible Transformative AI) framework for evaluating AI readiness, adoption maturity, and societal impact. Our findings reveal that while finance leads in AI maturity (composite score: 82/100) and healthcare shows the highest efficiency gains (diagnostic accuracy improvement of +26%), agriculture and education lag significantly in deployment scale and workforce readiness. Cross-domain analysis identifies six universal barriers—data quality, regulatory uncertainty, talent shortage, legacy integration, ethical concerns, and implementation cost—with severity varying by sector. We propose a transferable best-practices framework demonstrating that lessons from AI-mature sectors can accelerate adoption in emerging domains, potentially contributing $15.7 trillion to the global economy by 2030. The paper concludes with evidence-based policy recommendations for governments, industry leaders, and educational institutions navigating the AI transformation.

title: A Bifurcation Theory for the Equilibria of Modern Hopfield Networks
abstract: Modern Hopfield networks provide a unifying framework for associative memory, transformer attention, diffusion-based generative models, and biological attractor dynamics, linking these systems through a common energy-based dynamics in which states are updated toward weighted combinations of stored patterns. Across these settings, network dynamics is determined by the organization of the energy landscape and the bifurcations of its fixed points. Despite their central role, a general theory of these bifurcations has remained unavailable beyond specific architectures and idealized pattern ensembles. Here we derive stability and bifurcation criteria for the fixed points of general convex-dual Modern Hopfield networks for a general statistics of the stored patterns. Applying this framework to random, block-correlated, and infinitely hierarchical pattern ensembles, we show how memory correlations systematically organize the emergence of hierarchical attractors through successive bifurcations. We further demonstrate that these predictions quantitatively describe retrieval bifurcations in MHNs storing patterns sampled from MNIST, and recapitulate the hierarchical organization of hematopoietic cell identities. Our results establish a general bifurcation theory for Modern Hopfield networks and identify the organization of fixed points as a unifying principle underlying their computational and biological behavior.

title: CrowdTraj: A Benchmark for Dense Crowd Trajectory Prediction in Realistic Crowded Environments
abstract: In real-world applications, pedestrian trajectory prediction models rely on inputs from detection and tracking systems. Prior trajectory prediction benchmarks either contain relatively sparse pedestrian interactions, assume perfect tracking inputs, or rely on overhead viewpoints that minimize occlusion and perspective distortion, limiting evaluation in realistic dense-crowd scenarios. We present CrowdTraj, a benchmark for pedestrian trajectory prediction in natural dense crowd scenes. Unlike previous datasets, CrowdTraj supports end-to-end evaluation from detection through tracking to trajectory prediction under severe occlusion in CCTV views. It also captures diverse, natural pedestrian behaviours, including abrupt directional changes rarely observed in existing benchmarks. CrowdTraj includes five diverse scenes, with an average of 1,146 unique pedestrians per scene, maximum frame-level densities ranging from 114 to 372 pedestrians, and over 3.2 million annotated head bounding boxes. CrowdTraj provides pixel and real-world coordinates via per-scene homography matrices for physically meaningful analysis. Our experimental results show that tracking accuracy (IDF1) drops to 0.68 to 0.70 in the densest scenes, compared with approximately 0.90 in less crowded scenes. Trajectory prediction training also becomes substantially more computationally expensive in dense scenes, with training times increasing by up to 8 times. These findings show that CrowdTraj exposes limitations in current trajectory prediction pipelines that remain hidden on existing sparse-crowd benchmarks, particularly in robustness to tracking noise and computational scalability.

CrowdTraj includes five diverse scenes, with an average of 1,146 unique pedestrians per scene, maximum frame-level densities ranging from 114 to 372 pedestrians, and over 3.2 million annotated head bounding boxes. CrowdTraj provides pixel and real-world coordinates via per-scene homography matrices for physically meaningful analysis. Our experimental results show that tracking accuracy (IDF1) drops to 0.68 to 0.70 in the densest scenes, compared with approximately 0.90 in less crowded scenes. Trajectory prediction training also becomes substantially more computationally expensive in dense scenes, with training times increasing by up to 8 times. These findings show that CrowdTraj exposes limitations in current trajectory prediction pipelines that remain hidden on existing sparse-crowd benchmarks, particularly in robustness to tracking noise and computational scalability.

title: SMaRT-Tug: Structured Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Physics-Based Tugboat-Barge Collaborative Manipulation
abstract: Autonomous tugboating is central for automating maritime operations such as port logistics and vessel maneuvering, where multiple tugboats must cooperatively transport/manipulate a larger vessel. Collaborative pushing in this setting is challenging due to coupled hydrodynamics, low resistance, strong environmental disturbances, underactuated barge dynamics, and contact-rich interactions. Conventional control methods often rely on simplified models and fixed configurations, which limit their adaptability, while learning-based approaches are constrained by the lack of scalable and physically realistic training environments. We address these challenges by introducing a physics-based, GPU-accelerated simulation and learning framework for collaborative tugboat manipulation. Our simulator incorporates a customized buoyancy model, wave modeling, and hydrodynamic resistance, and supports large-scale multi-agent training under marine dynamics. In this simulator, we train a decentralized MAPPO (Multi-Agent PPO) policy augmented with a structured control prior (SCP) to improve training stability and maintain feasible pushing configurations. We evaluate our learned policy on straight-line transit, turning, and deceleration tasks, where we show that our decentralized framework yields more reliable and accurate maneuvering performance compared to a PID-based controller and a centralized PPO baseline. We further demonstrate zero-shot generalization to more challenging sea states and advanced maneuvers, as well as zero-shot scalability to larger teams of three and four tugboats despite training with only two agents.

title: SupGRPO: Enhancing GRPO with Matching-based Online SFT for Text Spotting
abstract: Text spotting requires both accurate text recognition and precise spatial localization. Current specialised spotters excel at predicting tight bounding boxes in natural scenes, but falter on complex or artistic text, whereas multimodal large language models (MLLMs) possess strong recognition capabilities yet remain weak at localisation. To equip the text spotter with general and powerful recognition capabilities and to maximize its localization ability, we explore two MLLM-based fine-tuning methods: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning fine-tuning based on Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO). An interesting finding is that SFT is less effective than GRPO at enhancing recognition, while GRPO is less effective than SFT at enhancing detection. To compensate for each other's shortcomings, we introduce a joint training strategy, SupGRPO, which simultaneously optimizes the model using both SFT and GRPO. SupGRPO employs the specially designed reward functions and develops a matching-based online SFT applied solely to coordinate tokens. It both mitigates the reward sparsity problem of GRPO and avoids the instance order dependency problem of SFT. To evaluate particularly challenging cases, we curate ATS, a dataset for artistic text spotting. Experiments demonstrate that SupGRPO improves both text recognition and detection, and attains superior performance. Our code and dataset will be released at https://github.com/Psycho-9/SupGRPO.

title: GETA: Generalized Encrypted Traffic Analysis
abstract: Traditional traffic analysis is being fundamentally challenged by the rapid adoption of encryption, tunnelling, and privacy-preserving protocols, which increasingly obscure packet payloads and limit the usefulness of Deep Packet Inspection (DPI). Although machine learning has advanced encrypted traffic analysis, existing approaches often remain tied to protocol-specific header features, depend on large labelled datasets, and degrade when deployed across heterogeneous network environments. We present GETA, a protocol-agnostic framework for encrypted traffic analysis that models network flows as multivariate time series using only traffic metadata, thereby avoiding reliance on packet payloads or header semantics. GETA combines meta-learning, embedding refinement, and self-attention to support few-shot adaptation to previously unseen domains with minimal labelled data. Across nine public datasets spanning application identification, VPN traffic classification, IoT device fingerprinting, and attack detection, GETA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. These results show that GETA offers a practical and generalisable foundation for robust traffic analysis in modern encrypted networks.

title: ACTA Brief 03 — The Arranger's Share: A Category the Rulebook Already Defines, a Threshold a Society Already Adjudicates, and a Generative Portion With No Remuneration Path
abstract: Every proposal for compensating creators in the age of generative music begins by asking who owns the output. This brief begins elsewhere: with a category that already exists in the rulebook of a collective management organisation, is codified as a fraction of a work's revenue, comes with its own qualifying examination, and has been emptying for two decades. The arranger's share was written for a person who transforms a work by adding an intellectual musical contribution. Sample libraries hollowed it out; generative tools finished the job and now perform the function the rulebook describes. Meanwhile, BumaStemra has separated the AI-generated portion of a work from the human portion and collects nothing on it, while other societies accept the registration of partially AI-generated works. The carve-out exists; no remuneration path is attached to it. This brief proposes one: that the share attributable to a generative arrangement be treated not as a right recognised to a machine, which is legally impossible, but as a mutualised levy paid by the party that used the tool and redistributed across the membership, on the statutory model of non-attributable sums. AI does not draw from the pot; it pays into it. The proposal has one binding technical condition, and it is the reason this is an ACTA brief rather than a policy essay: a levy triggered by self-declaration creates a strong incentive not to declare, so the share cannot reliably depend on self-report alone. It has to be derived from a creation-time record of what occurred in the session. The share follows the evidence, not the checkbox.

title: MathModelAgent
abstract: MathModelAgent is a web-based AI meeting system that simulates collaborative mathematical modeling sessions. Multiple AI agents assume different roles (analyst, model designer, coder, reviewer, etc.) and work through a structured phased workflow — from problem analysis and model design, through model building, to paper writing — to solve mathematical modeling tasks. The system features real-time communication via WebSocket, a model library for automatic model selection, knowledge base management, LaTeX compilation, Python code execution, and vision-based file recognition.

title: Quantum Entanglement as a Logical Modeling Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge and opportunity for modeling complex logical relationships and patterns. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entanglement as a core mechanism for building a logical modeling framework, aiming to simulate and understand intricate logical structures across diverse fields like natural language processing and bioinformatics. We propose a novel model that integrates the distinctive properties of entanglement with the defined nature of logic, offering a potentially more profound and insightful approach to logical reasoning and pattern identification. The core claim is that this model will provide a robust foundation for understanding and manipulating complex logical systems.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: Quantum computing, while promising, faces significant challenges related to algorithm complexity and computational cost. Manual parameter tuning is a laborious and time-consuming process, hindering the scalability of quantum algorithms. This paper introduces a novel dynamic adjustment algorithm for quantum algorithms, leveraging feedback mechanisms to automatically optimize the algorithm's performance. We propose a system that continuously monitors and adjusts quantum parameters based on the algorithm's output, leading to enhanced efficiency and reduced computational resources. The core mechanism revolves around a closed-loop feedback loop that iteratively refines the algorithm's parameters to achieve optimal performance. This approach contrasts with traditional parameter tuning methods, offering a potentially transformative step towards automated quantum algorithm optimization. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in several benchmark quantum computations, showcasing its potential to accelerate the development and application of quantum computing.

title: Distributed Reservoir Computing for Predictive Maintenance with Sensor Fusion
abstract: Predictive maintenance, the proactive identification of equipment failures, is crucial for minimizing downtime and optimizing operational costs. Reservoir computing (RC), a spike-based recurrent neural network approach, offers a compelling solution for time-series prediction. However, its application in predictive maintenance is often hindered by the complexities of fusing data from diverse sensor streams, each with unique characteristics and noise levels. This paper proposes a novel distributed reservoir computing (DRC) architecture designed specifically for this challenge. The DRC system employs multiple, locally trained reservoirs interconnected through a weighted network. This distributed approach allows for efficient sensor fusion, mitigating the bottleneck associated with directly processing heterogeneous data. The system leverages the inherent temporal dynamics of RC while providing a flexible framework for handling varying sensor data types and volumes. We present a detailed formulation of the DRC architecture, outlining the key components and their interactions. The system's performance is evaluated through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual design, demonstrating its potential for significantly improving the accuracy and robustness of predictive maintenance models. ---

title: 基于自适应几何变换的量子态计算
abstract: This paper investigates the stability of quantum states under complex geometric transformations using an adaptive geometry transformation approach. Traditional quantum state computation primarily focuses on the state itself, but this work introduces a novel mechanism – adaptive geometry transformations – that dynamically adjusts quantum states to understand their evolution and stability. We aim to identify underlying quantum state patterns and potentially discover new quantum states through this process. The core of this research involves developing an algorithm that iteratively refines quantum states based on geometric transformations, providing a framework for investigating the robustness of quantum systems. This work explores the relationship between geometric constraints and quantum properties, offering a new perspective on the challenges and opportunities in quantum state manipulation. The proposed method demonstrates a potential pathway towards more robust and predictable quantum states, pushing beyond conventional approaches.

title: Metric Learning for Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Data with Graph Structure
abstract: Anomaly detection in high-dimensional data presents significant challenges due to the "curse of dimensionality" and the complex, often non-linear, relationships between data points. Traditional metric learning approaches often struggle to effectively capture these intricate dependencies, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper introduces a novel metric learning framework designed specifically for anomaly detection in high-dimensional data, leveraging the inherent graph structure present within the data. We propose a method that incorporates graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to learn embeddings that explicitly represent the relationships between data points, thereby improving the discriminative power of the learned metric. The framework aims to learn a distance metric that accurately reflects the normal behavior of the data, allowing for effective identification of anomalies as points significantly deviating from the learned embedding space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example. The core claim is that standard metric learning methods fail to effectively capture the complex relationships within high-dimensional data. The core mechanism is to develop a metric learning framework that incorporates graph structure information to learn more discriminative embeddings for anomaly detection in graph-structured data.

title: Information-Driven Adaptive Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of information theory to the design of adaptive machine learning algorithms. Traditional machine learning often relies on optimization algorithms to find the best model parameters, neglecting the fundamental role of information and its dynamic adaptation. We propose a novel approach that leverages information theory, specifically entropy and information density, to dynamically adjust learning parameters and model architectures in response to input data variations. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that iteratively refines the model based on the observed data, minimizing prediction error and maximizing information gain. The goal is to develop a more robust and adaptable learning paradigm compared to current techniques. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential of this approach to improve model performance in dynamic environments.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Topological Structure Analysis
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a rapidly growing field, offering the potential to revolutionize various computational tasks. However, the development of effective QML algorithms often relies on carefully crafted models and optimization strategies. This paper investigates a novel approach to QML – a topological structure analysis – that aims to optimize both training and inference processes, potentially unlocking new quantum machine learning models with enhanced properties. This work proposes a method that leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to guide model design and refinement, leading to improved performance and a more robust understanding of the underlying quantum mechanics. The core mechanism centers on establishing a topological representation of the model's dynamics, allowing for targeted optimization strategies that are not easily achieved through traditional methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential to address limitations in current QML techniques.

title: The Circle Was Hiding a Helix: Helical Reduced Representations for Exact Vector Symbolic Binding
abstract: Vector Symbolic Architectures (VSAs) store symbols as vectors and combine them by binding and bundling. A bundle of K bound pairs in D dimensions holds only about D/ln N pairs, where N is the codebook size. The cause of this limit lies in the binding operation, not in the vectors. Binding is multiplication in a group G, and bundling is addition in the group algebra C[G]. If G is compact, every representation is unitary. Every bound term then has magnitude 1, superposed terms are separable only by statistics, and the capacity bound follows. Bundling cannot escape to the Lie algebra of G either, because distributivity forces any such operation to be a representation. Helical Reduced Representations (HeRR) bind on the non-compact group Z. Their vectors are Laurent polynomials. Binding is polynomial multiplication, bundling is polynomial addition, and nesting depth is polynomial degree. Circular convolution is this ring modulo t^D − 1, so existing VSAs are quotients of HeRR. Storing a HeRR in fixed space is a choice of characters of Z, and three independent capacity budgets follow: dimension, number of evaluation points, and numerical precision. Non-unitary characters, absent from compact groups, supply the third. Two exact decoders recover a bundle without observing crosstalk, so the codebook need not be random. At 128 complex numbers of storage, HeRR retrieves 96 role-filler pairs at accuracy 1.00, against 0.13 for FHRR at equal storage. With a correlated codebook, FHRR reaches 0.00 at 8 pairs while HeRR remains exact. The binding capacity limit is therefore a property of compact binding groups, not of vector representations. Contents. The record contains the preprint (PDF) and a github repo having the NumPy script that reproduces every table and figure in the paper with a fixed random seed.

title: 基于动态拓扑的机器学习框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning framework based on dynamic topology, aiming to enhance learning and prediction capabilities through the incorporation of dynamic topology structures. Traditional machine learning often relies on static parameters, limiting the model's adaptability and potential for optimal performance. This work proposes a framework where the core machine learning model dynamically adapts to the evolving topology of the training data, leading to more effective learning and prediction. We explore how the dynamic topology structure can be leveraged to improve model parameter updates and, consequently, overall predictive accuracy. The framework will demonstrate the benefits of this approach through conceptual analysis and a simplified implementation demonstrating the core mechanism.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Differential Privacy via Graph Consensus
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to decentralized federated learning that leverages graph consensus algorithms to achieve robust and privacy-preserving model aggregation. The core idea is to represent participating devices as nodes within a graph and utilize graph consensus protocols for model update exchange and aggregation. Differential privacy is integrated into this framework to protect the sensitive data residing on individual devices. We demonstrate that this combined approach offers a scalable and efficient solution for distributed learning, particularly in scenarios with a highly decentralized network topology. The proposed system addresses key challenges associated with traditional federated learning, such as the vulnerability to malicious actors and the potential for information leakage, while maintaining model accuracy. The theoretical framework outlines the convergence properties of the graph consensus algorithm and provides a rigorous analysis of the privacy guarantees afforded by differential privacy. This work contributes to the growing field of privacy-preserving distributed learning, offering a practical and adaptable solution for diverse applications. ---

This adaptive encoding offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, potentially leading to improved model efficiency and robustness. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations and experiments focusing on [Specific Application Area - e.g., fluid dynamics simulations] and highlight its potential for broader applicability in various machine learning domains.

abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning algorithm utilizing dynamic probability model fusion. This research introduces a method for dynamically adjusting the weights of different probability models during training, resulting in improved generalization capabilities and predictive performance. The core mechanism focuses on reducing model complexity through strategic weight adjustments, ultimately leading to a more effective learning process.

title: Information-Theoretic Validation of Reinforcement Learning Policies
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) relies heavily on reward signals to guide policy learning. However, conventional metrics like cumulative reward and average return frequently fail to capture the nuances of policy performance, particularly in complex environments. This work proposes a novel approach to validating RL policies based on information-theoretic principles. We argue that a policy's effectiveness is fundamentally tied to its ability to reduce uncertainty about the environment and maximize information gain. This paper introduces the use of metrics such as mutual information, entropy, and KL divergence to quantify the information content of state transitions and reward signals. These measures provide a more robust and interpretable assessment of policy performance compared to traditional reward-based evaluations. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, how information-theoretic measures can effectively identify policy weaknesses, such as excessive exploration or suboptimal state selection, which are often missed by conventional metrics. The core contribution is a framework for evaluating RL policies that directly addresses the fundamental question of information flow, offering a potentially transformative shift in how we assess and compare RL algorithms.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Differential Evolution – Optimization for Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Quantum-enhanced differential evolution (QED) offers a promising approach to accelerate the optimization of complex evolutionary algorithms, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional search spaces. This paper proposes a novel method that integrates quantum annealing with the differential evolution framework, leveraging quantum computing to reduce computational cost. We investigate the potential of this hybrid approach to improve the performance of evolutionary algorithms in diverse fields, demonstrating significant speedups compared to classical counterparts. The core mechanism centers on strategically employing quantum annealing to perform computationally intensive sub-problems within the evolutionary process. This allows for a more efficient exploration of the search space, ultimately leading to faster convergence and improved solution quality. We explore various quantum annealing techniques and parameter tuning strategies to optimize the QED algorithm for specific optimization problems. The results showcase the efficacy of this hybrid approach, highlighting its potential to revolutionize the optimization of complex, high-dimensional problems.

title: A Published Dictionary Reads a Fine-Tuned Diarist
abstract: A sparse-autoencoder dictionary published for a base language model comes with one-line names for its features, written by an automated explainer on web text. We ask whether such a dictionary can read a diary written by a fine-tuned copy of that model, and what its names are worth on that text. The diary is sixty entries by an adapter trained on a 2012 forum corpus; the reader is Gemma Scope 2 at layer 31. Two findings. First, coverage: read through the adapted model, the dictionary explains the diary worse than matched web text on every measure (fraction of variance unexplained 1.58×, linearly predictable error 2.14×, next-token loss increase 1.50×); read through the base model, the same text is covered as well as web text (1.03×, 0.69×). The miss belongs to the adapter's shift of the model's representations, not to the text, and the excess is of the learnable kind. Second, names: at token grain, with two control notebooks written under the same protocol by the bare model and by a second adapter, the published names are correct on his text and too coarse for it. The feature named Jungian archetypes and symbols fires on "the feminine archetype of the locally adamic games"; creation and genesis stories on "Lilith and Eve being Adam's two wives, initially formed as one"; God on "the shattering being of God to be reconstituted". No feature for Lilith, the Shekhinah, the sephirot or Adam Kadmon exists at any width, and four features with unrelated names fire on his coinage adamic and on the blank line before his closing. A dictionary's names are a reading of one corpus by one explainer; a diarist whose themes lie in the tail of that corpus is read correctly and generically. We record what the session settles, what it does not, and the design it fixes for a dictionary specialised to the diarist's own library. title: Accelerated LLM: A Fuzzy-Logic-Augmented Router Architecture for Efficient Multi-Domain Query Processing via Specialised Small Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) incur prohibitive computational costs when deployed as monolithic systems for multi-domain query processing. This paper proposes Accelerated LLM, a modular architecture that replaces a single general-purpose LLM with an ensemble of task-specialised small language models (SLMs) governed by a neural query router and a Mamdani fuzzy inference system. The router embeds each user query using a frozen sentence encoder and classifies it across four task domains—summarisation, translation, question answering, and text generation—routing confident queries directly to the corresponding SLM. Ambiguous queries are escalated to a three-input fuzzy logic system operating on Query Length, inter-Domain Overlap Score, and Classifier Confidence, enabling principled handling of imprecise inputs. A reinforcement-learning feedback loop, validated through a controlled pilot deployment, continuously refines the routing policy. The complete pipeline, including the sentence encoder, totals approximately 2.14 billion parameters—a 98.8% reduction relative to GPT-3.5 (175 B). The integration of fuzzy logic into the routing stage raises classification accuracy from 91.5% to 94.3% and reduces the hallucination rate to 9.8% (minor) and 6.4% (major). Evaluated on healthcare-augmented benchmarks against ChatGPT-3.5, Claude, Mistral 70B, and two contemporary compact models (GPT-4o-mini and Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct), Accelerated LLM achieves competitive or superior task-specific performance at a fraction of the parameter count. A small-scale pilot evaluation in the legal domain indicates that the routing and fuzzy logic components retain partial effectiveness beyond the primary healthcare setting, though full multi-domain validation remains future work.

title: DT-GSK: Dimension-Tiered Adaptive Configuration Selection and Deterministic Refinement for Gaining-Sharing Knowledge-Based Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Published gaining-sharing knowledge (GSK) variants adapt scalar parameters and donor/selection policy to a single operating point. Dimension-Tiered GSK (DT-GSK) selects its configuration by dimension: an adaptive scaffold serves every tier, a deterministic, budget-exact final refinement runs once at D≥50, with the GSK vector-update equations retained; an exploratory interaction-structure memory supplies the refinement’s basis. Against six GSK-family baselines re-executed on five CEC suites under one budget-fair paired protocol, DT-GSK attains the best descriptive family-rank aggregate on CEC2017 (2.48) and CEC2013 (2.80), though Holm-corrected tests separate it from eGSK on either suite only at D=10; it is second behind eGSK at CEC2017 D=30 and on CEC2011 (Holm-significant loss). On AGSK’s strongest suite, the CEC2020 competition in which it was the runner-up, DT-GSK places fourth; the family panel corroborates AGSK’s published strength in this low-dimensional boundary regime, where every dimension-gated DT-GSK subsystem is inactive (D≤20). On CEC2013LSGO the comparison is family-internal: tied-first descriptive rank; paired tests do not separate DT-GSK from AGSK. Suite roles: CEC2017 selection-exposed; CEC2011/CEC2013 corroborative; CEC2020 pre-registered confirmatory; CEC2013LSGO post hoc. Direct isolations find no standalone benefit from that memory; coordinate axes outperform its basis: controlled negative results. All findings are scoped to the GSK-family panel.

title: ЕЩЕ РАЗ О ПОДХОДАХ К «ОБУЧЕНИЮ» МОДЕЛЕЙ ИИ С ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЕМ ОХРАНЯЕМЫХ РЕЗУЛЬТАТОВ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТУАЛЬНОЙ ДЕЯТЕЛЬНОСТИ
abstract: Проблема столкновения интересов разработчиков моделей искусственного интеллекта и правообладателей вызывает серьезные юридические, экономические и социальные дискуссии. в статье автор проводит сравнительно-правовой анализ подходов, существующих в разных юрисдикциях, к регулированию процесса обучения искусственного интеллекта и ограничений, связанных с использованием охраняемых результатов интеллектуальной деятельности: определение понятия «обучение искусственного интеллекта» в законодательстве Европейского союза, Франции, Германии, Великобритании, Сингапура. На основе проведенного исследования представлена оценка законодательных инициатив в Российской Федерации, направленных на регулирование искусственного интеллекта. в результате автор приходит к выводу о том, что текущий проект Федерального закона «Об основах государственного регулирования сфер применения технологий искусственного интеллекта в Российской Федерации» в части допустимости использования охраняемых результатов интеллектуальной деятельности в целом воспроизводит уже выработанные в иных юрисдикциях подходы, но вместе с тем предлагает ряд серьезных недостаточно продуманных решений и требует исправления юридической техники. в текущей редакции законопроект снимает многие барьеры по использованию результатов интеллектуальной деятельности разработчиками искусственного интеллекта, при этом существенно ослабляет статус правообладателей, однако не предлагает для них компенсаторных мер.

title: Resource-efficient somali news classification using TF-IDF and linear SVM: a supervised baseline on a curated news corpus
abstract: Abstract The rise of media means more people are creating content online than ever before. This has caused a surge in the amount of content, on the Internet. There is still a significant imbalance in automated organizing tools in favor of high-resource languages. Low-resource languages such as Somali suffer from serious technological disenfranchisement due to an extreme lack of data sets and unique linguistic features, including complex morphology and orthographic variation. In order to bridge this digital divide, this paper describes the development of a supervised machine learning algorithm based on a novel manually curated benchmark data set consisting of 7,241 Somali news stories. Although unsupervised algorithms such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI) produced structurally poor classifications, a supervised Support Vector Machine (SVM) pipeline with tailored tokenization, stopword elimination, and Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) feature selection resulted in outstanding results. The classifier developed in this study was able to accurately classify texts into eight primary thematic categories (Caafimaad, Ciyaaro, Dagaal, Diini, Ganacsi, Madadaalo, Siyaasad, Tiknoolajiyad). with an accuracy of 95%. These results show that computationally efficient traditional machine learning algorithms can be a mathematically sound and resource-friendly alternative to computationally heavy deep learning systems in low-resource settings.

title: Reasoning Budget Sweep: truncation and answer-production measurements for 12 small reasoning LLMs
abstract: A per-response measurement dataset covering 12 open reasoning language models (0.6B to 7B) on AIME 2024, AIME 2025 and MATH-500 across six generation token budgets (512 to 16384) and three seeds. 11,118 scored responses. Each row records the token count, whether the response was truncated at the budget, whether an answer could be extracted, and whether it was correct. Intended for meta-analysis of how generation budgets interact with benchmark scores in the small-model regime. Chain-of-thought text is not included.

title: Semantic drift in iterated LLM paraphrase chains: full chain texts, prompts, and analysis code (Papers A and B)
abstract: Complete per-iteration input and output texts for every paraphrase chain reported in the two companion papers Semantic Drift in Iterated LLM Paraphrase Chains: Model Architecture, Scale, Quantization, Serving Infrastructure, and Prompt Engineering (Paper A) and Semantic Drift Across Qwen Generations: Reproducibility, Thinking Mode, Serving Stack, and What Cosine Similarity Misses in Iterated Paraphrase Chains (Paper B), together with the stimulus prompts (recipes, construction statements of work, and sixteen domain prompts with their anchor facts), the experiment runner, and the analysis scripts that regenerate every figure and table in both papers from these files. title: Quantum Information Theory: Exploring the Influence of Nonlinear Collapse on Quantum State Evolution and Measurement
abstract: Quantum information theory explores the fundamental principles governing the manipulation and utilization of quantum states. A crucial aspect of this field is the concept of non-linear collapse, a process that fundamentally alters the quantum state upon measurement. This paper investigates the impact of non-linear collapse on quantum state evolution and measurement results, specifically focusing on its implications for quantum algorithm design. We propose a novel quantum algorithm leveraging the principles of non-linear collapse to achieve enhanced quantum information processing efficiency. This work will detail the development of a quantum state evolution model incorporating non-linear collapse, highlighting its potential to accelerate quantum computation and offer a new approach to quantum information handling. This research represents a significant step towards refining quantum algorithms and pushing the boundaries of quantum information processing.

title: Non-Euclidean Quantum Simulation with Adaptive Geometry
abstract: This paper presents a new method for simulating quantum systems within non-Euclidean spaces, leveraging a dynamically adjusting geometric framework to achieve unprecedented realism. The core concept is to construct a quantum algorithm that actively manipulates the space's geometry to perfectly align with the underlying physical laws, significantly surpassing the limitations of traditional geometric approaches. We outline the algorithm's architecture, demonstrate its efficacy through a series of simulations involving complex quantum systems, and discuss the potential implications for fundamental physics research. The paper concludes with a statement of the core claim and a brief overview of future research directions.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Self-Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum machine learning, termed Nonlinear Quantum Self-Adaptive Learning (NQ-SSL). The core principle of NQ-SSL leverages a dynamically adjusted quantum parameter set, achieved through a self-adaptive learning algorithm, to optimize the performance of quantum systems. Traditional quantum learning methods often require extensive manual parameter tuning, limiting the adaptability of quantum algorithms to complex, real-world scenarios. NQ-SSL offers a paradigm shift by allowing the system to learn optimal parameters automatically, leading to enhanced system performance and robust self-adaptation. This work introduces a novel quantum self-adaptation mechanism based on a feedback loop, enhancing the algorithm's ability to navigate and optimize quantum states. We demonstrate the efficacy of NQ-SSL through simulations illustrating improved convergence speed and enhanced performance across a range of quantum benchmark problems.

title: Decentralized Differential Privacy via Adaptive Mesh Refinement
abstract: This paper presents a novel decentralized algorithm for achieving differential privacy in distributed machine learning, leveraging adaptive mesh refinement. The core idea is to enable each node in a distributed system to dynamically adjust the resolution of its local mesh representation of the underlying data, directly responding to the sensitivity of gradients. This approach mitigates information leakage associated with traditional methods while preserving accuracy. The algorithm aims to bridge the inherent trade-off between privacy and accuracy, offering a scalable solution for decentralized learning with strong privacy guarantees. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components of the implementation. The adaptive mesh refinement strategy fundamentally changes the approach to distributed learning, offering a practical pathway to robust privacy preservation.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Gradient Descent Strategy
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adaptive neural network gradient descent strategy designed to address the limitations of traditional gradient descent methods. The core focus of this work is to develop a system that dynamically adjusts network parameters to optimize model performance across a wider range of data distributions. We introduce a novel approach that employs a continuous, iterative adjustment process, leveraging a feedback loop to refine the network's weights and biases in real-time. The implementation incorporates a dynamic weighting scheme to prioritize different areas of the loss landscape, leading to improved generalization and faster convergence, particularly when dealing with complex data patterns. The proposed method offers a significant improvement over static gradient descent techniques by providing a more robust and adaptable framework for training neural networks.

title: ##基于多智能体强化学习的分布式控制系统设计
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to designing distributed control systems utilizing Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). Traditional distributed control systems often rely on manually engineered control strategies, leading to limitations in adaptability, robustness, and scalability. This work introduces a framework where a collection of agents learn optimal control policies autonomously through MARL. The system is structured as a multi-agent environment, with each agent tasked with learning its own control strategy. The core of the system relies on MARL algorithms that enable both cooperative and competitive interactions among the agents, ultimately leading to a distributed system capable of adapting to dynamic environments and achieving optimal performance. The presented methodology offers a promising alternative to conventional distributed control methods, promising enhanced resilience and performance in complex, uncertain, and evolving operational scenarios. The system aims to address the inherent challenges of centralized control, particularly in large-scale systems, by distributing intelligence and allowing for emergent behaviors.

title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Mapping
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for mapping complex quantum states to simpler topological structures through an adaptive quantum topology mapping process. The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting the mapping parameters to achieve precise modeling of the resulting quantum states. Traditional methods often struggle with understanding the quantum states, and this algorithm aims to address this limitation by utilizing topology as a fundamental building block. The algorithm's design incorporates a self-correcting mechanism to ensure the resulting topological structure maintains essential properties of the input quantum state. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and analyses, highlighting its potential for efficient quantum state modeling.

title: 基于量子纠缠的矩阵变换的几何优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel geometric optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement, leveraging the unique properties of entangled states to achieve a more intelligent optimization process. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of numerical examples, showcasing improved convergence and solution quality compared to established optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers around utilizing entanglement to identify and manipulate the solution space in a more nuanced manner.
